quickAnswer: Clinton tops the 50 towns we serve for homes built in 1939 or earlier (40.0%) and for homes in multi-unit buildings (48.1%), and it ranks 2nd for renter households (44.4%).
body: ## The most pre-1940 housing of the 50 towns

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) counts 7,101 housing units in Clinton, and 2,838 of them, 40.0%, were built in 1939 or earlier. No other town we serve has a bigger share. The middle town sits at 16.6%. The median Clinton home dates to 1955, the second-oldest median of the 50 towns, against 1975 for the middle town. Only 287 units, 4.0%, have been added since 2010.

A house of that age raises plain questions about heat, such as how old the boiler is and whether the piping still matches the radiators. The answers differ from house to house. With 2,838 units dating from 1939 or earlier, a boiler or furnace in Clinton is more likely than in most towns to be heating a building that was designed around a different generation of equipment, so the piping and chimney get a look before a new unit is chosen.
## A mill town on the Nashua River

Clinton was first settled in 1654 as part of Lancaster and was incorporated as a separate town on March 14, 1850. It is named after the DeWitt Clinton Hotel in New York, a favorite of the founders, Erastus Brigham Bigelow and his brother Horatio. The town became an industrialized mill town, drawing water power from the Nashua River, and by 1890 it was noted for carpets and woven wire. Railroads came to serve that industry.

Construction on the Wachusett Dam began in 1897, and filling the Wachusett Reservoir in 1908 flooded a substantial portion of Clinton and neighboring towns, which had to be relocated. The town is small, 7.3 square miles, and 21.78% of that area is water. The Nashua River runs through it, and the large Wachusett Reservoir lies to the south of the town center. Clinton also claims the oldest continuously used baseball field in the world, Fuller Field, created in 1878. The ACS counts 2,838 units from 1939 or earlier.
## Nearly half of homes share a roof with another household

Multi-unit buildings hold 3,416 Clinton homes, 48.1% of the total and the highest share of the 50 towns. Single-family detached houses, at 39.9% of units, are the lowest share of any town on our list. The middle town has 76.7% detached. Heating a building with several households is a different job from heating a house, and the same goes for cooling and air quality.
## High rental share, low home values

Renters make up 44.4% of Clinton households (2,989 of 6,732), the 2nd-highest share, against 16.4% for the middle town. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $329,300, the lowest of the 50 towns and well under the $579,150 of the middle town. A replacement system is a significant decision at any price point, which is why the estimate is put in writing and comes before the work.
## Gas, oil and electricity all in play

Clinton does not lean on a single fuel. Utility gas heats 2,570 occupied homes (38.2%), fuel oil 2,031 (30.2%), electricity 1,483 (22.0%) and bottled gas 571 (8.5%). That variety means a replacement can start from a different place at each address. Oil ranks 30th of 50 for share and utility gas 28th, while electricity ranks 5th and bottled gas 10th. The details are on our [heating page](/cities/clinton/heating-installation-repair).
## The electric utility

National Grid supplies the electricity here: the town is on its Massachusetts Electric Company territory list. That makes Mass Save the first program to check for a heat pump, and the 2026 figures sit on the [heat pump page](/cities/clinton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Why does Clinton have so many apartments and multi-family buildings?
faq.a: The ACS shows that 48.1% of Clinton's homes are in multi-unit buildings, the highest share of the 50 towns, but it does not say why. For heating, a multi-unit building often means one boiler serves several households, which changes how a replacement is planned.

faq.q: How many Clinton households rent their home?
faq.a: The ACS 2022 counts 2,989 renter households out of 6,732, or 44.4%, the 2nd-highest share of the 50 towns. The middle town is at 16.4%. The other 3,743 households (55.6%) own, so a landlord decides about heat in 44.4% of the occupied homes.

faq.q: Does the age of Clinton housing change which system I should install?
faq.a: Often. With 40.0% of units built in 1939 or earlier, older construction can differ from newer construction in its piping, ducts and insulation. Sizing the equipment to the building matters more than the brand, and a heat loss calculation comes before the quote.

faq.q: Which fuel heats the most homes in Clinton?
faq.a: Utility gas does, at 2,570 occupied homes (38.2%), followed by fuel oil at 2,031 (30.2%) and electricity at 1,483 (22.0%). Electricity ranks 5th of 50 towns for share, so electric-heated homes are a bigger group here than in most places we serve.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Utility gas heats 38.2% of Clinton homes, oil 30.2%, electricity 22.0% and bottled gas 8.5%. With 3,416 homes in multi-unit buildings, a failed boiler in a shared building can leave several households cold at once.
body: ## No single dominant fuel

The ACS 2022 shows gas heating 2,570 occupied Clinton homes and fuel oil 2,031. Electricity heats 1,483 (22.0%), a share that ranks 5th of 50, and bottled or tank gas heats 571. Gas sits below the 41.9% of the middle town. Replacing a boiler or furnace here starts with finding out what the building has now and what the street can supply.
## Two- to four-unit buildings

Clinton has 692 homes in two-unit buildings (9.7%) and 1,112 in buildings of three or four units (15.7%). In a building that size one boiler may serve every household, so the days a building can be without heat shape how a job is planned. Our [Clinton overview](/cities/clinton) covers the wider housing picture.
## The old end of the stock

Clinton has the biggest share of pre-1940 housing in the 50 towns: 2,838 units, 40.0%. A median year built of 1955 puts the town second-oldest. In a building of that age, the radiators, the chimney and the existing piping decide a lot about which replacement fits, and a drawing of the current layout saves time at the estimate.
## What an estimate looks at
- Which fuels are practical at this address.
- Whether radiators, baseboard or ducts carry the heat.
- The size of the building's heat loss.
- Venting and the gas piping.
## Paperwork for gas equipment
A new gas boiler or furnace has to be permitted by a licensed plumber or gas fitter and passed by an inspector. Ask the town's building department if a job is unusual.
## Tenants

Clinton's 2,989 renter households are covered by the State Sanitary Code, which sets 68 F as the heating-season daytime floor and 64 F as the overnight floor (105 CMR 410.201). The landlord covers heat unless the lease says otherwise. This is general information, not legal advice.
## If the heat is out
Phone (508) 786-8755 at any hour. Emergency calls are answered around the clock, and a free written estimate arrives before work starts.

faq.q: Should I convert my Clinton oil boiler to gas?
faq.a: Only if gas is available on your street, which you should confirm early. Gas is the most common fuel in Clinton at 38.2% of homes and oil follows at 30.2%. A heat pump is a third option for some houses.

faq.q: One boiler heats my whole three-family. What should I plan for?
faq.a: The system, the piping and the access all shape the scope, and a shared boiler serves several households at once, so ask about the days the building may be without heat. The written estimate spells out the scope.

faq.q: My Clinton house is electric. Is that unusual?
faq.a: Not here. Electricity heats 22.0% of occupied homes, 5th-highest of the 50 towns, against 10.1% for the middle town. Resistance heat is often worth pricing against a heat pump, which does heating and cooling.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Only 39.9% of Clinton homes are single-family detached houses, and 22.7% sit in buildings of five or more units. Outdoor equipment can be hard to place at an apartment, so ductless units and permission from the owner or association matter.
body: ## Cooling a town of apartments and attached homes

Clinton has 2,830 detached houses, 749 attached townhouses (10.5%) and 1,612 units in buildings of five or more (22.7%). It also has 106 mobile homes (1.5%). That mix is unusual among the towns we serve. Detached houses can usually take an outdoor condenser. Apartments and townhouses may not, because of space or building rules, which is where ductless systems and permission from the owner or association come in.
## Options for different buildings
- **Ducted central air:** works where sound ductwork already exists and has room for the airflow.
- **Ductless mini-split:** cools one room or several without ductwork, and is often considered where ducts are missing or hard to reach.
- **Heat pump:** one system for heating and cooling, discussed on the [heat pump page](/cities/clinton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
- **Window units:** a common starting point, though they block a window and can be less efficient than a permanently installed system.
## Older buildings

Many older homes were built without central air, and older construction can make running new ducts difficult. In a multi-family building an owner may prefer separate small systems for each unit so each household controls its own comfort.
## Newer buildings in a very old town

Not everything here is old. The ACS counts 1,352 units from 1980 to 1999 (19.0%) and 684 from 2000 or later (9.6%), of which 287 date from 2010. Whether any of them has ducts that suit central cooling is something to check in the building, not assume from the year.
## Small multi-family buildings

The 692 units in two-unit buildings and 1,112 in three- and four-unit buildings raise the question of who owns the outdoor space. A shared yard, a common electrical panel and a tenant's right to a comfortable unit all enter the plan.
## Sizing
A cooling system that is too big cycles on and off and does a poor job of removing humidity. One that is too small runs constantly. Sizing should come from the building, not from the old unit.
## Repairs

If cooling stops, look at the thermostat, the breaker and the filter first. A frozen coil or a tripped outdoor disconnect can also stop it. If those are fine, call (508) 786-8755 and a technician can look for the fault.

faq.q: Can I cool an apartment in an older Clinton building without ducts?
faq.a: Often yes, with a ductless mini-split. It uses a small indoor unit connected to an outdoor unit by a thin line. Check with the owner or association first, because outdoor equipment is usually subject to building rules.

faq.q: Is a window unit good enough?
faq.a: It can be, for one room and a modest budget. A permanent system usually does a better job and keeps the window usable, but it costs more up front and may need permission.

faq.q: Can a Clinton mobile home use a mini-split?
faq.a: Often, since a mini-split needs no ducts. The ACS 2022 counts 106 mobile homes in town (1.5%). The load, the electrical service and the placement of the outdoor unit decide the details.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Clinton is in National Grid territory, so Mass Save is the first program to check. Electricity already heats 1,483 homes (22.0%), and 5,065 units (71.3%) were built before 1980, so weatherization status shapes most projects.
body: ## National Grid and the program

National Grid serves Clinton, which puts Mass Save in play. Its 2026 whole-home heat pump rebate pays $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, to houses that are already weatherized. The full conditions live on the [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
## Which Clinton homes are candidates

Electricity heats 1,483 Clinton homes (22.0%), the 5th-highest share of the 50 towns. Bottled or tank gas heats another 571, and oil heats 2,031. For a house on electric resistance a heat pump is worth pricing. For a propane house it is worth comparing against the cost of the fuel. Homes on gas or oil can also use one, often with the old system kept as a backup.
## Age against the weatherization test

The 684 units built in 2000 or later (9.6%) meet the age route outright, and 287 of those date from 2010. At the other end, 2,838 units go back to 1939 or earlier. A Home Energy Assessment, which tells how much weatherization work stands in the way, may be part of the process for many homes here.
## Buildings, not just houses

Detached houses are only 2,830 of Clinton's 7,101 units. The remainder is 749 townhouses plus the two- to four-unit buildings and the large complexes. In a multi-unit building each household may want its own head or system, and with one whole-home rebate per customer account it is worth asking early how a rebate would apply.
## Mobile homes and small buildings
The ACS counts 106 mobile homes. They have small footprints, little room for ducts and their own electrical limits, so a ductless unit is a common thing to price there.
## Fuel costs and the existing system

Gas heats 2,570 occupied homes (38.2%) and oil heats 2,031 (30.2%). In a gas house a heat pump may go in alongside the existing system rather than replace it. An oil house is where the swap is most often on the table, since the boiler and the tank are both candidates for replacement at once.
## Sizing
We assess the heating load before quoting. The [air conditioning page](/cities/clinton/air-conditioning-installation-repair) covers the cooling side.

faq.q: Is the Mass Save heat pump rebate available in Clinton?
faq.a: Clinton is in National Grid's territory, so Mass Save is the program to look at. The home has to meet its weatherization test and the installer has to be eligible. Terms can change, so confirm at masssave.com.

faq.q: Do I need an energy assessment first?
faq.a: For the whole-home rebate, you may. Anything built before 2000 has to show a Home Energy Assessment with under $1,000 of recommended work, or finished earlier recommendations. Clinton has 5,065 units built before 1980.

faq.q: Can a heat pump work in an old Clinton house?
faq.a: It can, depending on insulation, air leakage and sizing. We assess the heating load first. Some old houses use a heat pump for most of the load and keep the existing system as a backup.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Clinton has 3,743 owner-occupied households and 2,989 renter households. Owners schedule their own tune-ups, while renters depend on a landlord, and a median build year of 1955 makes yearly service a sensible habit.
body: ## Who arranges the service

Owners hold 55.6% of Clinton households (3,743) and renters hold the rest. In an owner-occupied house the owner decides when to service the equipment. In a rental the landlord has to book it, and a visit ahead of the cold weather is the cheapest protection against a cold-snap failure.
## The routine for each fuel

Oil heats 2,031 Clinton homes, and an oil unit wants cleaning every year. Gas, at 2,570 homes, calls for a yearly look at the burner and the safety controls. Bottled gas ranks 10th of 50 for share and its equipment gets the same checks. Heat pumps need clean filters and a clear outdoor unit. Electricity heats 1,483 homes, and resistance equipment has few moving parts but still needs its wiring and controls tested.
## How old is the equipment?

The median Clinton home was built in 1955. Another 1,008 units date from 1940 to 1959 and 1,219 from 1960 to 1979. A boiler in a house that age may have been there a long time, and a tune-up is also the moment to find out how much life is left.
## What a visit can include
- Burner and combustion check on oil and gas equipment.
- Filter, blower and coil inspection.
- Flue and venting inspection, a safety item.
- Thermostat and control tests.
- Condensate drain and outdoor unit checks on cooling equipment.
## Shared boilers

Where one boiler heats several households, as it can in the 1,112 units in three- and four-unit buildings, a visit before the cold weather protects everyone on the system. A single worn part can shut down heat for the whole building.
## Older buildings and surprises

Clinton's pre-1940 units number 2,838, and chimneys, flues and old piping in buildings that age deserve a closer look than the burner alone. A visit may turn up a cracked liner, a leaking joint or a vent that no longer matches the equipment. When it does, the estimate for the fix is written and free before anyone starts.
## Seasons
Heating work fits late summer and early fall, and cooling work fits spring. Call (508) 786-8755 to book. The [Clinton overview](/cities/clinton) has the housing figures.

faq.q: How often should a Clinton landlord service a boiler?
faq.a: Once a year, before the heating season. Boilers in rentals fail in cold snaps, and an annual visit can catch a worn part early.

faq.q: What does an oil tune-up involve?
faq.a: A technician typically cleans the combustion area, inspects the burner, checks the filter and tests the controls. The goal is reliable operation through winter, and the visit can also show whether the boiler is nearing the end of its life.

faq.q: Is it worth servicing a heat pump in a Clinton apartment?
faq.a: Yes, in a lighter way. Filters need regular cleaning and the outdoor unit must stay clear of leaves and snow. With 2,989 renter households in town, ask the landlord or association who is responsible for the work.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Clinton mixes very old buildings with newer ones, 19.0% of units dating from 1980 to 1999. Leaky old buildings and tight new ones raise different air quality questions.
body: ## Old and new air problems side by side

Clinton's 1980 to 1999 band holds 1,352 units (19.0%), and 287 units (4.0%) date from 2010 or later. Next to the largest pre-1940 share of the 50 towns, these later buildings may behave differently. A leaky older building lets pollutants thin out, and it also lets in dust, pollen and cellar air. Newer, tighter buildings hold moisture and fumes unless ventilation works.
## Multi-unit buildings

Multi-unit buildings, which hold 48.1% of Clinton homes, often share walls, and some share ducts or basements. Odors, smoke or moisture can travel between units in some buildings. A ventilation or filtration fix often has to consider the whole building rather than a single apartment.
## Vacant units

Cooking exhaust, bathroom fans and dryer vents are the usual places where moisture and fumes should leave a building. The ACS counts 369 vacant units in Clinton, a 5.2% vacancy rate. A unit that sits empty for a time can build up stale air and humidity if the system is not running, though how much depends on the building.
## Water around the town

The town's area is 21.78% water, and the Nashua River runs through it with the Wachusett Reservoir south of the center. Whether any of that matters to a given basement is a question for the basement itself, since moisture sources are specific to a building.
## Checklist
- **Ductwork:** leaky or dusty ducts matter more than most people expect.
- **Combustion safety:** flues need an occasional inspection, and every sleeping area should have a carbon monoxide alarm.
- **Ductwork:** leaks and debris can matter, and cleaning helps in some cases.
- **Combustion safety:** vented equipment should be checked, and carbon monoxide alarms are worth having.
## Fuel-burning equipment

With 2,570 gas and 2,031 oil homes in the ACS, plenty of Clinton heating equipment sends combustion products up a flue. A yearly check of the vent and a working alarm in every sleeping area are the basics.
## Renters and air

With 2,989 renter households, many Clinton residents cannot change a duct or a fan on their own. A tenant can still raise a ventilation or moisture problem with the landlord in writing, and keep a copy.
## Next step
Call (508) 786-8755 to book an assessment. The [heat pump page](/cities/clinton/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers related equipment.

faq.q: Can smells travel between apartments in a Clinton building?
faq.a: In some buildings they can, through shared ducts, gaps around pipes and shared basements. Sealing, ventilation and filtration can help, and the right fix depends on the building.
Not always. If a basement or a room feels damp, a dehumidifier can help, but it is better to find the source of moisture too.

faq.q: Does a very old building need different air quality steps?
faq.a: It can. With 2,838 Clinton units dating from 1939 or earlier, many buildings leak air in ways that newer ones do not. Start with fans, filters and a visual check for damp, and bring in a technician for ducts or combustion equipment.
